👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Timer bar relies on a `shownAt` field the payload doesn't have, and the spec never adds it (confidence high)**

The spec says the bar is "driven by CSS from the payload's `shownAt`". `CaptureToastPayload` has no such field (`apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/types/screenshot-capture.ts:234-247`). The "The window" section, which lists what changes in main, doesn't add it either.

The timestamp is also hard to pin down. Main starts the timer when the renderer reports ready, not when `show` runs (`capture-toast-window.ts:119-125`, `:159-160`). A re-target or a pointer leaving the card restarts the full timeout (`:170-175`). So a `shownAt` taken in `show` would drift from the real timer.

Suggested fix: either add the field to the window changes, saying when main stamps it (on ready, on resume), or drive the bar only from the payload's arrival plus the hover state. The thumbnail change also needs listing: the 160 px limit is set in `screenshot-ipc.ts:131` and the payload doc comment says "at most 160 px wide", but the spec doesn't name either spot.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The "Copied · ⌘V" pill is macOS-only, but the card ships on Windows too (confidence medium)**

The summary, the acceptance criteria (line 84) and the mockup all show the resting pill as **Copied · ⌘V**. Line 87 also asks the card to reveal files in Explorer on Windows, so the card is meant for Windows as well. The spec doesn't say the shortcut hint changes per platform (Ctrl+V on Windows), or that the i18n key takes the shortcut as a parameter.

The pill labels also differ between sections: decision 6 uses "Copied ✓", the summary "Copied · ⌘V", and the mockup's failed-vault card plain "Copied". Pinning down one label per state (at rest, after pressing Copy) would make the `capture-toast.test.tsx` assertions clear.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Make the live hover state available to keyboard users.** Keyboard focus does not reveal the hover state, and the invisible Edit button remains in the tab order. Make the card focusable and apply the hover styles and animation pause on `:focus-within`. Based on learnings: interactive elements must not rely solely on mouse hover to reveal controls.

So keyboard focus cannot reach it, and the mockup mirrors that. Keyboard access to the card is out of scope (spec "Out of scope": shortcuts on the card).

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "The timer channel above" points to text that comes below, inside the actions list (confidence high)**

The `screenshot:toast-timer` channel is first described at lines 133-136, in "The card (renderer)", which comes after this line. So "above" points the reader the wrong way. The bullet also sits in the list under "**Two new actions.**" (`CAPTURE_TOAST_ACTIONS`), but a main→card message is not an action. The section opens with "gains two things" (line 113) and now lists a third. Suggested fix: give the channel its own top-level bullet in "The window" (shape `{ remainingMs: number | null }`, when main sends it, and the `desktop/ipc-contract.mdx` row), and have the renderer section refer back to it.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · 🟡📝 **Consider · docs: The list of timer events misses Edit waiting on a Save, so the bar would keep draining while the card stays (confidence high)**

The bar only mirrors main's timer. The spec lists when main sends `screenshot:toast-timer` as "renderer ready, re-target, pointer in, pointer out". Main also stops the timer in a fifth case: when Edit (today Annotate) is pressed while that shot's Save is still writing (`capture-toast-window.ts:211-216`). After that, `resume` returns early while that wait is pending (`:172`), so a pointer out does not restart the timer. If the timer is built from this list, no `null` is sent in that case. The bar would then drain to zero and the card would stay on screen. Suggested fix: say that every `stopTimer`/`restartTimer` in main sends the message, or add "Edit waiting on a Save" to the list.

<!-- wachi:finding -->

👮 **Wachiman** · **Looks addressed** at `f86dc4b`: Fixed: the bar now mirrors `screenshot:toast-timer` `{ remainingMs | null }`, and the payload no longer needs a timestamp. Two smaller points are still open. First, the list of when main sends it misses Annotate/Edit waiting on a Save (`capture-toast-window.ts:211-216`); see the new finding. Second, the thumbnail aside: `TOAST_THUMBNAIL_WIDTH = 160` in `screenshot-ipc.ts:131` and the "at most 160 px wide" doc comment in `shared/types/screenshot-capture.ts:235` are still not named in the spec.
